notes: Scam patterns written from public police/SEBI advisories and news reports of Indian investment fraud. Each scam has ordered stages so the app can say where the user is and what comes next.

scams.name: WhatsApp/Telegram stock-tips group with fake trading app
scams.summary: You are added to a 'VIP' stock-tips group run by a fake 'professor' or 'assistant' of a famous broker. After weeks of free tips and fake profit screenshots from other 'members', you are moved to a trading app or website that shows fake profits. When you try to withdraw, they ask for tax or fees.

stages.name: Hook
stages.signs: Ad on Instagram/Facebook/Telegram, or added to a group without asking. Free stock tips, 'learn trading' sessions.
stages.next: They will share daily tips and screenshots of other members' profits to build trust.

stages.name: Trust building
stages.signs: Daily classes, a 'professor' or 'mentor', many members posting profit screenshots, small tips that seem to work.
stages.next: They will ask you to open an account on 'their' platform or app, often called an institutional or VIP account.

stages.name: Move to fake app
stages.signs: App link that is not on Play Store/App Store, an APK file, or a website that looks like a real broker. 'Institutional account', 'OTC trades', 'block deals'.
stages.next: They will ask for a first deposit to a UPI ID or bank account, and show quick profits in the app.

stages.name: First deposit
stages.signs: Money sent to a personal UPI ID or a company account that is not the broker's. App shows big profits. Sometimes a small withdrawal is allowed to win trust.
stages.next: They will push you to invest much more: guaranteed IPO allotment, a 'loan' or 'credit' inside the app, limited-time offers.

stages.name: Pressure to invest more
stages.signs: IPO allotment 'guaranteed', in-app loan you must repay, threats that your account will be frozen, urgency.
stages.next: When you try to withdraw, they will block it and demand tax, fees or 'unlock charges'.

stages.name: Withdrawal blocked
stages.signs: Asked to pay 'income tax', 'service fee', 'margin', 'unfreeze charges' before you can withdraw.
stages.next: Every payment leads to a new fee. Then the group and app disappear.

stages.name: Vanished
stages.signs: Group deleted, numbers blocked, app not opening.
stages.next: Report immediately. Do not pay 'recovery agents' who promise to get your money back; that is a second scam.

scams.name: Fake IPO allotment / institutional account offer
scams.summary: You are promised guaranteed IPO allotment, 'institutional quota', 'OTC' or 'block deal' shares at a discount through a special account. Real IPO allotment is never guaranteed and is done only through your own broker or bank (ASBA).

stages.name: Offer
stages.next: They will ask you to open a special account or pay into a UPI/bank account.

stages.name: Payment
stages.signs: Paying to a personal UPI or an unrelated company account instead of applying via your own broker or bank.
stages.next: The app will show allotment and big gains, then ask you to pay more to 'subscribe' or 'clear dues'.

stages.name: Dues and withdrawal fees
stages.signs: Told you owe money for extra allotted shares, or must pay tax to withdraw.
stages.next: Each payment leads to another demand, then contact stops.

scams.name: Part-time 'task' job that turns into investment
scams.summary: You are offered easy money for liking videos or writing reviews. After small payouts, you are asked to 'prepay' for higher tasks or invest to unlock earnings.

stages.name: Easy task
stages.signs: Like YouTube videos, rate hotels, earn ₹50–₹200 per task.
stages.next: They will pay you a small amount to win trust, then move you to a Telegram group.

stages.name: Prepaid tasks
stages.signs: 'Merchant tasks' or 'VIP tasks' where you must pay first to earn a bigger return.
stages.next: Your balance will show profit but be 'locked' until you complete more paid tasks.

stages.name: Locked balance
stages.signs: Told you made a mistake and must pay to recover, or pay to withdraw.
stages.next: Each payment is followed by a bigger one. Stop paying now.

scams.name: Crypto / forex / USDT trading platform
scams.summary: A 'mentor' or online friend introduces a crypto, forex or USDT platform (often MT4/MT5 based) with daily returns. Many such forex platforms are not authorised in India, and the RBI keeps a public alert list of unauthorised forex platforms.

stages.name: Introduction
stages.signs: Online friend, dating match or mentor talks about crypto or forex profits.
stages.next: They will guide you to a website or app and ask you to buy USDT or deposit.

stages.name: Deposit and fake gains
stages.signs: Deposits via UPI/P2P to individuals; dashboard shows fast gains.
stages.next: They will push bigger deposits for 'VIP level' or special signals.

stages.name: Withdrawal blocked
stages.signs: Asked to pay tax, 'anti-money-laundering' fee or account upgrade to withdraw.
stages.next: The platform disappears after collecting fees.

scams.name: Ponzi / 'daily return' app with referral income
scams.summary: An app or scheme promises fixed daily or monthly returns and extra income for adding friends. Early members are paid using new members' money until it collapses.

stages.name: Join
stages.signs: Fixed daily/monthly return, 'plans' of ₹5,000/₹10,000, team or level income.
stages.next: Small returns will be paid at first to make you invest more and bring friends.

stages.name: Grow the team
stages.signs: Pressure to recruit, bonuses for referrals, bigger plans.
stages.next: Withdrawals will slow down with excuses like server upgrade or tax.

stages.name: Collapse
stages.next: Report with transaction details; collect details from others who lost money.

first_hour_steps: Call 1930 (National Cyber Crime Helpline) immediately. Reporting fast gives the best chance of the money being frozen before it is moved.
File a complaint at cybercrime.gov.in with every transaction ID (UTR), amount, date-time, and the UPI ID or bank account you paid to.
Call your bank's customer care, report the transactions as fraud, and ask them to raise a dispute.
Do not pay any more 'tax', 'fees' or 'unlock charges'. They are part of the scam.
Keep screenshots of chats, the group, the app and all payments. Do not delete the chats.
Ignore anyone offering to recover your money for a fee. That is a second scam.
